prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick questions so my advice is useful:

- How serious were your injuries (minor sprain, broken bones, hospitalization)?  
- When did the crash happen? (This matters for the statute of limitations.)  
- Were there clear facts of fault (police report, other driver admitted fault, witnesses)?  
- Do you already have medical bills, lost wages, or insurance communications?  
- Do you want a lawyer who will litigate (go to trial) or are you expecting a negotiated settlement?

If you’d rather skip questions, I can give general, practical guidance you can use now.

What to do right away
- Get medical care and follow the provider’s instructions — important for health and for your claim.  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, injuries, scene, contact info for witnesses, police report number.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without an attorney. Give basic facts to your own insurer as required.  
- Keep copies of medical bills, pay stubs, rental car receipts, and anything else related to the crash.

How to choose the right personal-injury lawyer
Look for an attorney or firm that:
- Specializes in car-accident / personal-injury cases (not mainly family law, criminal, etc.).  
- Has experience handling cases like yours (severity, liability issues, catastrophes).  
- Works on contingency (no fees unless you recover money). Typical contingency fees range ~33–40% depending on case stage. Confirm how costs (expert fees, filing fees) are handled.  
- Has trial experience or a record of taking cases to court when insurers lowball.  
- Is local or regularly practices in Alameda County (Pleasanton/Dublin/Livermore) — familiarity with local judges, courts, and medical providers helps.  
- Has clear communication: responsive, explains strategy, provides a written fee agreement.  
- Good reviews and no major disciplinary history (you can check the State Bar of California).

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled many Pleasanton/Alameda County car-accident cases? How many?  
- What results have you obtained for cases like mine? Any settlements/verdicts you can share?  
- Who exactly will handle my case (partner, associate, paralegal)? Who will I speak with day-to-day?  
- What is your fee and how do you handle costs?  
- What is your strategy for my case and likely timeline?  
- Do you anticipate taking the case to trial if needed?  
- Can you provide references from past clients?

Red flags
- Pressuring you to sign quickly.  
- Promises of a specific result.  
- No written fee agreement.  
- Poor communication during the intake.

Legal timing to know
- In California, the general statute of limitations for personal injury is 2 years from the date of injury (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. § 335.1). (Claims against public entities have much shorter notice periods.) If your accident was recent, acting soon is important.

Next steps I can do for you
- If you want, I can research and provide a short list (3–6) of personal-injury lawyers or firms that handle car-accident cases near Pleasanton with ratings, quick notes on experience, and contact info.  
- Or I can draft an email or phone script you can use for initial consultations.

Tell me which you prefer and any answers to the questions above, and I’ll proceed.
